'''Faustin-Archange Touadéra''' ({{IPA|fr|fostɛ̃ aʁkɑ̃ʒ twadeʁa|lang}}; born 21 April 1957) is a Central African politician and [[mathematician]] who has been [[List of heads of state of the Central African Republic|president of the Central African Republic]] since March 2016, and was previously [[List of heads of government of the Central African Republic|its prime minister]] from 2008 to 2013. He was elected to the presidency at the [[2015–16 Central African general election|2015–16 general election]], in a second round of voting against former prime minister [[Anicet Georges Dologuélé]]. He was re-elected for a second term at the [[2020–21 Central African general election|2020–21 election]] and a third term at the [[2025 Central African general election|2025 Central African election]], both of which took place amid low voter turnout and political violence.<ref>{{cite news |work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |title=Provisional election results show Central Africa Republic President Faustin Archange Touadéra won a third term |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/provisional-election-results-show-central-africa-republic-president-128930514 |date=6 January 2025 |access-date=15 January 2026 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |work=[[France24]] |title=Central African Republic's Touadera wins third presidential term |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260105-central-african-republic-president-touadera-re-elected-with-over-76-of-vote |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=15 January 2026 }}</ref>

Since at least 2023, Touadéra has been backed by the [[Wagner Group]], a [[Federal Government of Russia|Russian]] state-sponsored [[private military company]] financing his elections and [[Russian disinformation|launching disinformation campaigns]] for him while intimidating his opponents.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|title=Russia's Wagner Group and the sustainment of authoritarianism in Africa: Implications for China at home and abroad|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/13523260.2025.2474763|journal=Contemporary Security Policy|date=2025|issn=1352-3260|pages=497–521|volume=46|issue=3|doi=10.1080/13523260.2025.2474763|first=Christopher|last=Spearin|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Wagner-backed CAR leader asks voters to abolish term limits|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-66353281|date=30 July 2023|work=BBC News|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref> During his rule, which included the removal of term limits after the contested [[2023 Central African constitutional referendum]] and the controversial 2025 general election,<ref name="Koena">{{Cite news |title=Central African Republic President Faustin Archange Touadéra reelected, provisional results show |url=https://apnews.com/article/central-african-republic-election-touadera-586cdbe64c133ff9d5251694fb43ce18 |last1=Koena |first1=Jean-Fernand |last2=Adetayo |first2=Ope |work=AP News |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=6 January 2026 |archive-date=6 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106141606/https://apnews.com/article/central-african-republic-election-touadera-586cdbe64c133ff9d5251694fb43ce18 |url-status=live}}</ref> his government has repressed opposition in the country.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Central African Republic: Concerns Over Crucial Election |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/11/28/central-african-republic-concerns-over-crucial-election |date=28 November 2025 |website=Human Rights Watch|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref>

== Early life ==

Faustin-Archange Touadéra was born in [[Bangui]]<ref name="Fridolin Ngoulou2016">{{cite web|url=http://rjdh.org/qui-est-le-nouveau-president-centrafricain-faustin-archange-touadera/|language=fr|title=Qui est le nouveau président centrafricain Faustin Archange Touadera ?|publisher=RJDH|date=22 February 2016|author=Ngoulou, Fridolin|access-date=27 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301074423/http://rjdh.org/qui-est-le-nouveau-president-centrafricain-faustin-archange-touadera/|archive-date=1 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> (then in [[Ubangi-Shari]] and now in the [[Central African Republic]]) on 21 April 1957,<ref name=":0" /> the son of a driver and a farmer.<ref name=":0">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.jeuneafrique.com/304420/politique/centrafrique-5-choses-a-savoir-sur-faustin-arcange-touadera/|title=Centrafrique : cinq choses à savoir sur Faustin-Archange Touadéra|language=fr|date=22 February 2016|magazine=Jeune Afrique|author=Duhem, Vincent|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref> His family was originally from [[Damara, Central African Republic|Damara]].<ref>Tshitenge Lubabu M. K., {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120911055011/http://www.jeuneafrique.com/jeune_afrique/article_jeune_afrique.asp?art_cle=LIN15068faustardauo0|title="Faustin-Archange Touadéra"}}, ''Jeune Afrique'', 15 June 2008 {{in lang|fr}}.</ref> He received his secondary education at the [[Lycée Barthélémy Boganda de Bangui|Barthelemy Boganda College]] in Bangui and obtained a baccalaureate in 1976,<ref name="Fridolin Ngoulou2016"/> before attending the [[University of Bangui]] and the [[University of Abidjan]]. He earned a [[doctorate]] in [[mathematics]] in 1986, supervised by Daniel Gourdin at the [[Lille University of Science and Technology]] (Lille I) in France,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Touadera|first=Faustin|url=http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=8211537|title=Problème de Cauchy matriciels C∞ et dans les espaces de Sobolev à caractéristiques multiples}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis
|title=Matrix Cauchy problems with multiple characteristics in C∞ and Sobolev spaces
|publisher=Université Lille I
|year=1986
|type=Thèse de 3e cycle (Doctoral thesis)
|url=http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=8211537
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921061517/http://cat.inist.fr/?aModele=afficheN&cpsidt=8211537

|archive-date=21 September 2013
}}</ref> and another doctorate, also in mathematics and supervised by Marcel Dossa,<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.univ-orleans.fr/mapmo/imhotep/index.php?lang=en

|title=IMHOTEP
|access-date=3 May 2012
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921060852/http://www.univ-orleans.fr/mapmo/imhotep/index.php?lang=en

|archive-date=21 September 2013
|url-status=dead
}}</ref> at the [[University of Yaoundé I|University of Yaoundé]] in Cameroon in 2004.<ref name=":1" />

== Academic career ==

In 1987, Touadéra became assistant lecturer of mathematics at the [[University of Bangui]] and was vice-dean of the University's Faculty of Science from 1989 to 1992.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Central African Republic swears in new president|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2016/3/30/central-african-republic-swears-in-new-president|access-date=22 January 2021|website=Al Jazeera}}</ref> In the latter year he became director of the teachers' training college. He joined the Inter-State Committee for the Standardisation of Mathematics Programs in the French-speaking countries and the Indian Ocean (CIEHPM) in 1999, serving as the president of the Committee from 2001 to 2003. He became vice chancellor of the [[University of Bangui]] in May 2004.<ref name=":0" />

Touadéra subsequently served as rector of the university from 2005 to 2008, during which time he launched several key initiatives, such as the entrepreneurship training program and the creation of the [[Euclid Consortium]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Erisman|first=Al|date=1 October 2007|title=Update: Return to the Central African Republic|url=https://ethix.org/2007/10/01/return-to-the-central-african-republic|access-date=21 January 2021|website=Ethix.org}}</ref>

== Prime minister ==

Touadéra was appointed prime minister by President [[François Bozizé]] on 22 January 2008, following the resignation of [[Élie Doté]].<ref>[http://www.jeuneafrique.com/fluxafp/fil_info.asp?reg_id=0&art_cle=42184 "Centrafrique: le recteur de l'université de Bangui nommé Premier ministre"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521232703/http://www.jeuneafrique.com/fluxafp/fil_info.asp?reg_id=0&art_cle=42184 |date=21 May 2011 }}, AFP, 22 January 2008 {{in lang|fr}}.</ref> His government, composed of 29 members&mdash;four ministers of state, 17 ministers, and seven minister delegates, along with himself&mdash;was appointed on 28 January.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bozize|first=François|date=28 January 2008|title=Décret 08.025 du 28 Janvier 2008, portant nomination des Members du Gouvernement et ses modificatifs subséquents|work=Journal Official de la Republique Centrafricaine|url=|access-date=|language=fr}}</ref> A national dialogue was held in December 2008, and François Bozizé then dissolved Touadéra's government on 18 January 2009 in preparation for the formation of a government of national unity.<ref>{{Cite news|date=18 January 2009|title=Central African Republic president dissolves government|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2009-01-19/central-african-republic-president-dissolves/270016|access-date=21 January 2021|website=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]]|agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]}}</ref>

Touadéra was reappointed prime minister on 19 January. Later on the same day, his new 31-minister government was appointed, with only 10 ministers retaining their posts; many former rebels were included in the new line-up to prepare the country for the 2009 local elections and the 2010 presidential and parliamentary polls.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bozize|first=François|date=19 January 2009|title=Décret n°09.018 du 19 janvier 2009, portant nomination des membres du Gouvernement|work=Journal Official de la Republique Centrafricaine}}</ref>

Following a peace deal between the Bozizé government and the [[Séléka]] rebel coalition in January 2013, Bozizé dismissed Touadéra on 12 January 2013, in accordance with the terms of the agreement, which required that a new prime minister be appointed from the political opposition.<ref>{{Cite news|agency=[[Agence France-Presse]]|title=Central African opposition names Tiangaye as new PM|url=https://www.modernghana.com/news/439339/central-african-opposition-names-tiangaye-as-new.html|access-date=21 January 2021|website=Modern Ghana}}</ref> Later, Touadéra announced his intention to stand as an independent candidate in the [[2015–16 Central African general election]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=11 August 2015|title=Exiled Central African leader Bozize to stand at election|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozatp-uk-centralafrica-election-idAFKCN0QG0KA20150811|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

=== EUCLID involvement and High Steward ===

In 2008, the [[Euclid Consortium]] initiative hosted by the [[University of Bangui]] led to the formation of an intergovernmental university named [[EUCLID (Euclid University)|EUCLID]] (French: ''Pôle Universitaire Euclide''). In his capacity as prime minister, Touadera signed the instrument of participation for the Central African Republic in May 2010. His chief of cabinet [[Simplice Sarandji]] also signed the headquarters agreement for EUCLID in March 2011. In April 2012, Touadera personally presided over a graduation ceremony in New York, at the Permanent Mission of the Central African Republic to the United Nations, for a graduating diplomat of Burundi. After his tenure as prime minister, Touadera became EUCLID's High Steward, an honorary role.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euclid.int/news.asp|title=EUCLID News and Events|work=Euclid University}}</ref>

== President ==

=== Election ===

[[File:Secretary Pompeo meets with Central African Republic President Faustin-Archange Touadera (33709600898).jpg|thumb|Touadéra with US secretary of state [[Mike Pompeo]], 11 April 2019]]

Touadéra stood as a candidate in the December 2015&ndash;February 2016 presidential election. After finishing second in the first round of voting, he received the support of the majority of defeated candidates for the second round, which he won with 62% of the vote. He was sworn in on 30 March 2016. Speaking on the occasion, he vowed to pursue disarmament and "make CAR a united country, a country of peace, a country facing development".<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/article/us-centralafrica-president-idUSKCN0WW1ZG "Central African Republic's president vows peace, reforms at inauguration"], Reuters, 30 March 2016.</ref> He appointed [[Simplice Sarandji]] as prime minister on 2 April 2016. Sarandji was Touadéra's campaign manager during the election and Touadéra's chief of staff during his own time as prime minister.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2 April 2016|title=Central African president names PM in decree: radio|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-centralafrica-president-idUSKCN0WZ0Q3|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2 April 2016|title=Centrafrique : Sarandji nommé Premier ministre|url=https://www.bbc.com/afrique/region/2016/04/160402_car_pm|access-date=21 January 2021|work=BBC News Afrique|language=fr}}</ref>

=== Tenure ===

[[File:Vladimir Putin & Faustin Touadera - 2019.jpg|thumb|Touadéra with Russian President [[Vladimir Putin]] at the [[Russia–Africa Summit 2019|Russia–Africa Summit]] in Sochi on 23 October 2019]]

After Touadéra was sworn into office, France confirmed that it would end its military intervention in Central African Republic. France had around 2,500 troops deployed in the country as part of [[Operation Sangaris]], supporting about 10,000 [[United Nations]] [[United Nations peacekeeping|peacekeepers]].<ref name=Ibtimes>{{Cite news|last=Winsor|first=Morgan|date=30 March 2016|title=Central African Republic's New President Touadera In Uphill Battle Against Warring Muslim, Christian Militias|url=https://www.ibtimes.com/central-african-republics-new-president-touadera-uphill-battle-against-warring-muslim-2345672|access-date=21 January 2021|website=[[International Business Times]]}}</ref>

Without France's support, Touadéra  faced the immediate challenge of maintaining security in major cities.<ref name=Ibtimes/> The Central African Republic saw a 36 percent drop in its gross domestic product in 2013. The economy has slowly grown since then, but with the agricultural sector — the main contributor to GDP — still struggling, the government is struggling to raise revenue.<ref name="Ibtimes" />

In April 2022, CAR approved a plan to make [[Bitcoin]] an official currency in the country.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 April 2022 |title=Bitcoin becomes official currency in Central African Republic |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-61248809 |access-date=15 February 2025 }}</ref> At the time, it was the second country to make the cryptocurrency [[legal tender]] joining [[El Salvador]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Buck |first=Jonathan |date=30 April 2023 |title=The Fall Of Bitcoin In The Central African Republic: Why This Legal Tender Experiment Failed |url=https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/the-fall-of-bitcoin-in-the-central-african-republic:-why-this-legal-tender-experiment |access-date=14 February 2025 |work=Nasdaq}}</ref> The plan was abandoned in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Toppa |first=Sabrina |date=30 September 2023 |title=Why did the Central African Republic toss out bitcoin? |url=https://www.thestreet.com/crypto/policy/central-african-republic-bitcoin |access-date=15 February 2025 |website=TheStreet }}</ref> In December 2022, he attended the [[United States–Africa Leaders Summit 2022]] and met with US president [[Joe Biden]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 December 2022 |title=Africa: Heads of Delegation for U.S–Africa Leaders Summit – White House |url=https://allafrica.com/stories/202212130597.html |access-date=16 December 2022 |website=[[AllAfrica]] }}</ref>

Touadéra's personal security detail is reportedly composed of members of the Russian [[Wagner Group]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2018/08/russian-mercenaries-wagner-africa/568435/ |magazine=[[The Atlantic]] |quote=Wagner appears to have tapped this possibility at the highest level, reportedly serving as CAR President Faustin-Archange Touadera's personal security detail. |title=Russia's Favorite Mercenaries |date=27 August 2018 |first=Neil |last=Hauer}}</ref> In July 2023, Touadéra attended the [[2023 Russia–Africa Summit]] in Saint Petersburg and met Russian President [[Vladimir Putin]]. Touadéra expressed support for Russia, saying that Russia "had helped to save its democracy and prevent a civil war".<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 July 2023 |title=African leaders tell Putin: 'We have a right to call for peace' |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/putin-tells-african-leaders-moscow-is-studying-their-ukraine-proposal-2023-07-28/ |publisher=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

Also during the month, Touadéra called for a [[referendum]] to abolish [[term limit]]s (at the time set to two five-year terms), while also increasing the length of the term to seven years. Without the change, Touadéra would have been term-limited and ineligible to stand at the next presidential election. In order to hold the referendum, Touadéra sacked the head of the constitutional court in October 2022, which had previously ruled the referendum (boycotted by the opposition) unconstitutional.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 October 2022 |title=In Central African Republic, government removes two constitutional court judges after judgment seen as blocking president's plans to bypass term limits |url=https://constitutionnet.org/news/central-african-republic-government-removes-two-constitutional-court-judges-after-judgment |access-date=1 June 2023 |agency=Reuters |via=ConstitutionNet}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=5 June 2023 |title=République centrafricaine : Le référendum présente des risques |url=https://www.hrw.org/fr/news/2023/06/05/republique-centrafricaine-le-referendum-presente-des-risques |access-date=2 August 2023 |website=Human Rights Watch |language=fr}}</ref>

[[File:Le président et la première dame étaient présents aux paradex militaire qui avait eu lieu au camp KASSAï..jpg|thumb|President Touadéra with one of his two wives, First Lady [[Brigitte Touadéra]], at the 65th independence parade in 2025]]

In April 2024, Touadéra was received at the Elysée in France, for the second time since the start of his mandate in 2016, to sign a roadmap which will provide for the reestablishment of bilateral relations between the Central African Republic and France.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 April 2024 |title=Centrafrique Faustin-Archange Touadéra de nouveau reçu par Emmanuel Macron |url=https://www.africaintelligence.fr/afrique-centrale/2024/04/05/faustin-archange-touadera-de-nouveau-recu-par-emmanuel-macron,110201327-art |access-date=22 November 2024 |website=Africa Intelligence |language=fr}}</ref> In July 2025, he announced his reelection bid for president as the candidate of the [[United Hearts Movement]] in the [[2025 Central African general election]] scheduled in December.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 July 2025 |title=Central African Republic's President Touadera confirms third-term bid |url=https://www.africanews.com/2025/07/27/central-african-republics-president-touadera-confirms-third-term-bid/ |access-date=27 July 2025 |website=Africanews}}</ref>

On 10 February 2025, Touadera announced the creation of $CAR as the country's official [[meme coin]] describing it as an experiment in national development. The coin briefly reached a US$900 million market cap<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jha |first1=Prashant |title=Central African Republic's National Memecoin Hits $900M Market Cap—But Is It Real? |url=https://www.ccn.com/news/crypto/central-african-republic-national-car-memecoin-real/ |access-date=23 February 2025 |publisher=CCN |date=10 February 2025}}</ref> before experiencing a significant price drop of over 90%.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rukanga |first1=Basillioh |title=CAR leader launches meme-coin 'experiment' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cly5x0vpen8o |access-date=23 February 2025 |work=BBC News |date=11 February 2025}}</ref> In November 2025, the Constitutional Court authorized him to seek another term, despite opposition parties claiming that he does not meet the criteria for another election.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Koena |first1=Jean Fernand |last2=Banchereau |first2=Mark |title=Central African Republic leader cleared for third term in key vote followed closely by Russia |url=https://apnews.com/article/central-african-republic-touadera-russia-wagner-41891691b35cb17fac75159b78aa0d3e |access-date=14 November 2025 |work=AP NEWS |date=14 November 2025}}</ref> He subsequently won the election with around 76% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Central African Republic president wins third term by landslide |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0q40xg3j0jo |access-date=6 January 2026 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2025 general election, Touadéra repressed the political opposition in the Central African Republic, attempting to use the powers of the state to prevent opposition candidates from contesting in the election.<ref name=":02"/><ref name="AfricaNews">{{Cite news |title=Central African Republic President Touadéra wins third term: provisional results |url=https://www.africanews.com/2026/01/06/central-african-republic-president-touadera-wins-third-term-provisional-results/ |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=6 January 2026 |work=Africanews |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106142205/https://www.africanews.com/2026/01/06/central-african-republic-president-touadera-wins-third-term-provisional-results/ |archive-date=6 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Provisional results, which were announced on 6 January 2026,<ref name="Koena"/> showed that he won re-election with 76% of the votes,<ref name="RFI">{{Cite news |title=Central African Republic President Touadera wins re-election, results show |url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260106-central-african-republic-president-touadera-wins-re-election-results-show |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=6 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106154816/https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260106-central-african-republic-president-touadera-wins-re-election-results-show |archive-date=6 January 2026 |url-status=live |work=Radio France Internationale}}</ref> with a reported turnout among registered voters was 52.42%.<ref name="France24">{{Cite news |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260105-central-african-republic-president-touadera-re-elected-with-over-76-of-vote |title=Central African Republic's Touadera wins third presidential term |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=6 January 2026 |work=France24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106153515/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260105-central-african-republic-president-touadera-re-elected-with-over-76-of-vote |archive-date=6 January 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref> His opponents in the election disputed the results, citing alleged malpractice by the  [[National Authority of Elections]] (ANE) and widespread [[electoral fraud]].<ref name="BBC">{{Cite news |title=Central African Republic president wins third term by landslide |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0q40xg3j0jo |date=6 January 2026 |access-date=6 January 2026 |publisher=BBC News |last=Muia |first=Wycliffe |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260106111400/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0q40xg3j0jo |archive-date=6 January 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Anicet-Georges Dologuélé]] declared himself the winner of the election.<ref name="Koena" /> On 19 January 2026, the Constitutional Court officially declared Touadéra as the winner in the presidential race, having won 77.9% of the vote, followed by Dologuélé with 13.1%.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 19, 2026 |title=Central African Republic confirms Touadéra's election win despite fraud claims |url=https://apnews.com/article/central-african-republic-election-results-touadera-dologuele-66860f354854b90b1194f509746f190c |work=AP News}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

Touadéra was a [[deacon]] in a [[Baptist]] church of the Fraternal Union of Baptist Churches,<ref>Vincent Hugeux, [https://www.lexpress.fr/actualite/monde/faustin-archange-touadera-reconcilier-les-centrafricains_1795475.html Faustin-Archange Touadéra: "Réconcilier les Centrafricains"], lexpress.fr, France, 29 May 2016</ref> and is still a member of this union.<ref>Ornella K., [https://lavoixdafrique.info/republique-centrafricaine/centrafrique-s-e-touadera-implique-dans-la-promotion-de-la-culture-religieuse/ Centrafrique : S.E TOUADERA, impliqué dans la promotion de la culture religieuse] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128124051/https://lavoixdafrique.info/republique-centrafricaine/centrafrique-s-e-touadera-implique-dans-la-promotion-de-la-culture-religieuse/ |date=28 January 2023 }}, lavoixdafrique.info, 23 August 2022</ref> He is [[polygynous]] and married to two wives, [[Brigitte Touadéra]] and [[Tina Touadéra|Tina Marguerite Touadéra]].<ref name="koaci">{{cite news|date=20 March 2017|title=Centrafrique: Brigitte et Tina Touadéra, la bataille de l'ombre pour la place de première dame|work=Koaci.com|url=http://koaci.com/centrafrique-brigitte-tina-touadera-bataille-lombre-pour-place-premiere-dame-107495.html|access-date=29 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320160320/http://koaci.com/centrafrique-brigitte-tina-touadera-bataille-lombre-pour-place-premiere-dame-107495.html |archive-date=20 March 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Both Brigitte and Tina Touadéra have reportedly vied for the title and role of First Lady of the Central African Republic behind the scenes.<ref name="koaci" /> Touadéra has three children.<ref name="Fridolin Ngoulou2016" />
